intro.purpose: Compare one water-rich and one water-poor country using a world map. Analyse the data given for each country, such as rainfall, water sources, and population. Discuss how these factors affect water availability.

objectives.text: Compare one water-rich and one water-poor country using a world map and simple data.
Explain how rainfall, water sources and population affect water availability.
Understand why some places have plenty of water while others face shortages.

materials.text: Your two country cards: one water-rich country and one water-poor country
The data sheet for each country (G4_WATER_EO_DS_1). It is not part of this activity, so ask your teacher for it.
The Reflection Questions your teacher gives you (step 7). They are not part of the task card.

steps.text: Open Google Earth on your device.
Search for both countries on your cards—one water-rich and one water-poor.
Zoom in and look for water bodies like rivers, lakes, or coastlines.
Observe the landscape—is it green and forested, dry and desert-like, or mountainous?
Read the information on both country cards carefully.
With your group, compare these features:
Use the Reflection Questions to guide your discussion.
Write a short group report titled: “Why [Country A] is Water-Rich and [Country B] is Water-Poor”
items: 2–3 reasons why the first country has more water
2–3 reasons why the second country has less water
1 suggestion to help the water-poor country improve its water situation

steps.text: Present your report to the class.
Show your Google Earth map and point out water features.
Highlight the key facts and differences between the two countries.
